question: Can full meaning be understood from a sentence if one is only hearing a partial word?
premises: Understanding of the full meaning would have to come from the sentence as a whole.
If one claims it comes merely from that partial word, the hearer is no longer just a word-hearer.
The limited part would then no longer remain merely limited.
inference: Full sentential understanding cannot be reduced to hearing a mere fragment without contradiction.
uncertainties: The sentence continues into the next verse for its full conclusion.
plain_english: And how could he understand so much meaning from the sentence? If one says, 'just from that,' then he is not merely a hearer of a word, nor—
